criteria.text: Patient is 50 years of age or older
Prescribed by or in consultation with a neurologist
Beta-amyloid plaques verified by PET scan or CSF testing
Documented brain MRI within the last year showing no localized superficial siderosis, fewer than 4 brain microhemorrhages, and no brain hemorrhages greater than 1 cm in the past year
Objective evidence of cognitive impairment at screening
Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) global score of 0.5 or 1
Mini-Mental State Exam (MMSE) score of at least 22
Other known causes of dementia ruled out, including vascular dementia and Parkinson's disease dementia
Not taking blood thinners other than aspirin 81 mg or less
No brain hemorrhage, bleeding disorder, or cerebrovascular abnormalities in the last 6 months
No significant systemic illness or infection in the past 30 days
No unstable angina, myocardial infarction, advanced chronic heart failure, or clinically significant conduction abnormalities within 1 year prior to screening

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Leqembi (lecanemab-irmb) Criteria Version 1: Original 1/17/2023; Accepted 01/20/2023; Effective 03/01/2023.

Approval criteria 1-9 and denial criteria 2-5 encoded. Denial criterion 1 is failure to meet approval criteria. Treatment should be initiated at mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia stage of Alzheimer's disease; stage is notes only. The source describes accelerated approval and no safety or effectiveness data for initiation at earlier or later stages.

ARIA: enhanced clinical vigilance during the first 14 weeks. Symptoms suggestive of ARIA require clinical evaluation, including MRI if indicated. Common adverse reactions include infusion reactions, ARIA-Edema, headache, ARIA-H microhemorrhage and superficial siderosis. Cautions and monitoring remain notes only.

Initial approval: up to 3 months. Reauthorization: up to 6 months with MRI prior to the 5th dose showing no increase in size or number of ARIA, documented positive response, slowed rate of cognitive decline, and no adverse reactions. Additional MRIs before the 7th and 14th doses are required to screen for ARIA. Duration and reauthorization remain notes only.
Quantity per source label: 10 mg/kg infused over one hour once every two weeks; HCPCS J3590. Dosing and quantity enforcement remain notes only.

Aduhelm is a same-class anti-amyloid alternative, subject to its own criteria and separate evaluation. Kisunla is also a same-class anti-amyloid alternative, subject to its own criteria and separate evaluation. No oral step-therapy requirement is encoded.
